title: Structured investigation of the benefit of clinical photon-counting computed tomography in oncologic imaging
summary:
Computed tomography (CT) is an important method for creating images of the inside of the body, especially for cancer. There is a new CT technology called "photon-counting CT" (PCCT), which promises to deliver sharper images and potentially use less radiation. This new technique can measure the energy of X-rays more precisely, which could help to better distinguish between different types of tissue, such as tumor tissue.

In this study at the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), we want to investigate whether this new photon-counting CT technology actually offers advantages in routine clinical cancer imaging. To do this, we analyze the image data from patients who receive such a PCCT scan as part of their normal medical care.

No additional examinations or procedures are performed for this study. Participants simply receive the medically necessary CT scan. We then evaluate the quality of the images and assess how well tumors can be detected and characterized. The aim is to find out if photon-counting CT can improve cancer diagnosis and treatment planning in the future. Participation is only possible if the patient has previously given general consent for their data to be used for research purposes.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Clinically indicated photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) scan as part of routine clinical care at the Department of Radiology, DKFZ.
- Existing, valid informed consent from the patient for the scientific database (wDB) of the DKFZ, allowing the use of clinical and imaging data for research purposes.
Exclusion criteria:
- Missing, invalid, or withdrawn informed consent from the patient for the scientific database (wDB) of the DKFZ.
- Individuals without a clinical indication for an oncological CT examination (e.g., healthy volunteers).
- Persons unable to provide informed consent.
